items.decision_note: Messages 200 and 202 reportedly make the source-file handoff unconditional, but their verbatim text is not supplied here. Review whether a later MODIFY must remove the delivery_condition before the delivery claim.

The freelancer's 160-page statement conflicts with the opening client constraint of approximately 100 pages or fewer. Determine whether issue length should be an attribute of REQ_ISSUE_LAYOUT_ASSEMBLY with an AMBIGUOUS Event.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
After comparing all the options, I agree that the overall direction is good. Inter is cool, but it looks too thin. For article pages, we need a font that is easier to read and gentler on the eyes.

Here is a reference:

<https://forum.civicarchive.example/r/capitolarchive/comments/7m2qkx8/vintage_civic_review_spring_2004/#lightbox>

value_updates.body_font_treatment: Easy to read, gentle on the eyes, and not too thin

missing_event_candidate.description: The instruction to upload the pages version rather than the spread-preview version belongs to the narrower Heyzine upload-file selection Requirement.
The client changes the Heyzine workflow by taking responsibility for manually uploading the final PDF through the client's white-label account.

unresolved_candidate.description: The freelancer describes a 160-page magazine, while the opening project description says approximately 100 pages or fewer; the supplied messages do not contain a clear client confirmation of the final page-count constraint.
The freelancer proposes publication-wide punctuation normalization, but the client asks for clarification without clearly authorizing a complete copy-editing requirement.

The client says the issue would need to change to December after the missed launch window, but the exchange immediately returns to a same-day launch; whether the rendered issue date actually changed requires adjudication.
